sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi vimuñcan vibabhau tadā karṇaputro mahārāja varṣamāṇa ivāmbudaḥ
english: Then, loosing thousands of arrows, the son of Karṇa shone forth, O great king, like a raincloud pouring down its torrents.

sanskrit: tatas tu drupadānīkaṃ śaraiś chinnatanucchadam saṃprādravad raṇe rājan niśīthe bhairave sati
english: Then Drupada's host, its armor cleft asunder by his shafts, broke and fled in the battle, O king, in that dreadful hour of midnight.

sanskrit: pradīpair hi parityaktair jvaladbhis taiḥ samantataḥ vyarājata mahī rājan vītābhrā dyaur iva grahaiḥ
english: With the burning lamps cast away and blazing on every side, the earth gleamed, O king, like a cloudless sky studded with planets.

sanskrit: tathāṅgadair nipatitair vyarājata vasuṃdharā prāvṛṭkāle mahārāja vidyudbhir iva toyadaḥ
english: And with the fallen armlets the earth gleamed, O great king, as a raincloud gleams with lightning in the season of the rains.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇasutatrastāḥ somakā vipradudruvuḥ yathendrabhayavitrastā dānavās tārakāmaye
english: Then the Somakas, terrified by the son of Karṇa, fled in all directions, as the Dānavas, struck with fear of Indra, fled in the Tāraka war.

sanskrit: tenārdyamānāḥ samare dravamāṇāś ca somakāḥ vyarājanta mahārāja pradīpair avabhāsitāḥ
english: Tormented by him in battle and taking to flight, the Somakas shone forth, O great king, lit up by the lamps.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu nirjitya samare karṇaputro vyarocata madhyaṃdinam anuprāpto gharmāṃśur iva bhārata
english: Having vanquished them in battle, the son of Karṇa blazed forth like the sun, the hot-rayed one, reaching its noonday height, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: teṣu rājasahasreṣu tāvakeṣu pareṣu ca eka eva jvalaṃs tasthau vṛṣasenaḥ pratāpavān
english: Among those thousands of kings, both your own and the foe's, Vṛṣasena alone stood blazing in his might.

sanskrit: sa vijitya raṇe śūrān somakānāṃ mahārathān jagāma tvaritas tatra yatra rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having conquered in battle the brave great chariot-warriors of the Somakas, he hastened swiftly to where King Yudhiṣṭhira stood.

sanskrit: prativindhyam atha kruddhaṃ pradahantaṃ raṇe ripūn duḥśāsanas tava sutaḥ pratyudgacchan mahārathaḥ
english: Then your son Duḥśāsana, that great chariot-warrior, advanced to meet the enraged Prativindhya, who was consuming the foe in battle.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samāgamo rājaṃś citrarūpo babhūva ha vyapetajalade vyomni budhabhārgavayor iva
english: The encounter of those two, O king, was a wondrous sight, like that of Mercury and Venus in a cloudless sky.

sanskrit: prativindhyaṃ tu samare kurvāṇaṃ karma duṣkaram duḥśāsanas tribhir bāṇair lalāṭe samavidhyata
english: As Prativindhya was performing a deed hard to do in the battle, Duḥśāsana pierced him in the forehead with three arrows.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā putreṇa tava dhanvinā virarāja mahābāhuḥ saśṛṅga iva parvataḥ
english: Sorely wounded by your mighty son, the archer, the great-armed one shone forth like a mountain with its peak.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ tu samare prativindhyo mahārathaḥ navabhiḥ sāyakair viddhvā punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: But Prativindhya, that great chariot-warrior, having pierced Duḥśāsana in battle with nine shafts, struck him again with seven.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata putras te kṛtavān karma duṣkaram prativindhyahayān ugraiḥ pātayām āsa yac charaiḥ
english: There, O Bhārata, your son performed a deed hard to do, for he struck down Prativindhya's horses with his fierce arrows.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena dhvajaṃ ca samapātayat rathaṃ ca śataśo rājan vyadhamat tasya dhanvinaḥ
english: With a broad-headed shaft he brought down his charioteer and his banner, and shattered the chariot of that archer into a hundred pieces, O king.

sanskrit: patākāś ca sa tūṇīrān raśmīn yoktrāṇi cābhibho ciccheda tilaśaḥ kruddhaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: And the pennons, the quivers, the reins, and the traces, O lord, he cut to bits in his wrath with his smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: virathaḥ sa tu dharmātmā dhanuṣpāṇir avasthitaḥ ayodhayat tava sutaṃ kirañ śaraśatān bahūn
english: But that righteous one, robbed of his chariot, stood firm, bow in hand, and fought your son, showering forth many hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit: kṣurapreṇa dhanus tasya ciccheda kṛtahastavat athainaṃ daśabhir bhallaiś chinnadhanvānam ārdayat
english: With a razor-edged shaft he cut his bow, like one skilled of hand, and then, his bow severed, tormented him with ten broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā virathaṃ tatra bhrātaro 'sya mahārathāḥ anvavartanta vegena mahatyā senayā saha
english: Seeing him there bereft of his chariot, his brothers, those great chariot-warriors, came on with speed, together with a great army.

sanskrit: āplutaḥ sa tato yānaṃ sutasomasya bhāsvaram dhanur gṛhya mahārāja vivyādha tanayaṃ tava
english: Then he leaped onto the shining car of Sutasoma and, taking up a bow, O great king, pierced your son.

sanskrit: tatas tu tāvakāḥ sarve parivārya sutaṃ tava abhyavartanta saṃgrāme mahatyā senayā vṛtāḥ
english: Then all your warriors, surrounding your son, advanced into the fray, encompassed by a great army.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata niśīthe dāruṇe kāle yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: Then a battle broke out between your men and theirs, O Bhārata, in that dreadful hour of midnight, swelling the kingdom of Yama.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca nakulaṃ rabhasaṃ yuddhe nighnantaṃ vāhinīṃ tava abhyayāt saubalaḥ kruddhas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: As Nakula, furious in the fight, was slaying your host, the son of Subala rushed at him in wrath and cried, "Stand, stand!"

sanskrit: kṛtavairau tu tau vīrāv anyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇau śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Those two heroes, fixed in enmity and each longing for the other's death, struck at one another with arrows loosed from bows drawn to their full length.

sanskrit: yathaiva saubalaḥ kṣipraṃ śaravarṣāṇi muñcati tathaiva nakulo rājañ śikṣāṃ saṃdarśayan yudhi
english: Even as the son of Subala swiftly let fly his showers of arrows, so too did Nakula, O king, displaying his training in the fight.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau samare śūrau śarakaṇṭakinau tadā vyarājetāṃ mahārāja kaṇṭakair iva śālmalī
english: Both those heroes in the battle, bristling then with arrows, shone forth, O great king, like the silk-cotton tree with its thorns.

sanskrit: sujihmaṃ prekṣamāṇau ca rājan vivṛtalocanau krodhasaṃraktanayanau nirdahantau parasparam
english: Eyeing each other askance, O king, with eyes wide open and reddened with rage, they seemed to consume one another.

sanskrit: syālas tu tava saṃkruddho mādrīputraṃ hasann iva karṇinaikena vivyādha hṛdaye niśitena ha
english: But your brother-in-law, full of wrath, as if laughing, pierced the son of Mādrī in the heart with a single sharp barbed shaft.

sanskrit: nakulas tu bhṛśaṃ viddhaḥ syālena tava dhanvinā niṣasāda rathopasthe kaśmalaṃ cainam āviśat
english: Sorely wounded by your brother-in-law the archer, Nakula sank down upon the floor of his chariot, and a swoon came over him.

sanskrit: atyantavairiṇaṃ dṛptaṃ dṛṣṭvā śatruṃ tathāgatam nanāda śakunī rājaṃs tapānte jalado yathā
english: Seeing his bitter, arrogant foe brought to such a pass, Śakuni roared, O king, like a raincloud at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ nakulaḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ abhyayāt saubalaṃ bhūyo vyāttānana ivāntakaḥ
english: Then, regaining his senses, Nakula, the joy of Pāṇḍu, rushed once more at the son of Subala like Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: saṃkruddhaḥ śakuniṃ ṣaṣṭyā vivyādha bharatarṣabha punaś caiva śatenaiva nārācānāṃ stanāntare
english: In his wrath he pierced Śakuni with sixty shafts, O bull of the Bhāratas, and again with a full hundred iron arrows between the breasts.

sanskrit: tato 'sya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ muṣṭideśe sa cicchide dhvajaṃ ca tvaritaṃ chittvā rathād bhūmāv apātayat
english: Then he cut his arrow-laden bow at the grip, and swiftly cutting down his banner, he cast it from the chariot to the ground.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja rathopastha upāviśat taṃ visaṃjñaṃ nipatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā syālaṃ tavānagha apovāha rathenāśu sārathir dhvajinīmukhāt
english: Sorely wounded, O great king, he sank down upon the floor of his chariot; and seeing your brother-in-law fallen senseless, O blameless one, his charioteer swiftly bore him away by chariot from the front of the host.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcukruśuḥ pārthā ye ca teṣāṃ padānugāḥ nirjitya ca raṇe śatrūn nakulaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ abravīt sārathiṃ kruddho droṇānīkāya māṃ vaha
english: Then the Pārthas and their followers raised a shout; and Nakula, the scorcher of foes, having vanquished his enemies in battle, said wrathfully to his charioteer, "Bear me toward Droṇa's host."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā mādrīputrasya dhīmataḥ prāyāt tena raṇe rājan yena droṇo 'nvayudhyata
english: Hearing that word of the wise son of Mādrī, the charioteer drove on in the battle, O king, to where Droṇa was fighting.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ tu samare droṇaprepsuṃ viśāṃ pate kṛpaḥ śāradvato yattaḥ pratyudgacchat suvegitaḥ
english: But as Śikhaṇḍin sought to reach Droṇa in the battle, O lord of peoples, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat, intent and very swift, advanced to meet him.

sanskrit: gautamaṃ drutam āyāntaṃ droṇāntikam ariṃdamam vivyādha navabhir bhallaiḥ śikhaṇḍī prahasann iva
english: As the descendant of Gautama, that tamer of foes, came on swiftly toward Droṇa, Śikhaṇḍin, as if laughing, pierced him with nine broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: tam ācāryo mahārāja viddhvā pañcabhir āśugaiḥ punar vivyādha viṃśatyā putrāṇāṃ priyakṛt tava
english: The preceptor, O great king, having pierced him with five swift shafts, struck him again with twenty, that doer of good to your sons.

sanskrit: mahad yuddhaṃ tayor āsīd ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate yathā devāsure yuddhe śambarāmararājayoḥ
english: A great battle there was between those two, terrible in form, O lord of peoples, as in the war of gods and Asuras between Śambara and the king of the gods.

sanskrit: śarajālāvṛtaṃ vyoma cakratus tau mahārathau prakṛtyā ghorarūpaṃ tad āsīd ghorataraṃ punaḥ
english: Those two great chariot-warriors made the sky veiled with a web of arrows; the night, by nature terrible in aspect, became more terrible still.

sanskrit: rātriś ca bharataśreṣṭha yodhānāṃ yuddhaśālinām kālarātrinibhā hy āsīd ghorarūpā bhayāvahā
english: And the night, O best of the Bhāratas, was for the war-loving warriors like the Night of Doom, terrible in aspect and fraught with fear.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu mahārāja gautamasya mahad dhanuḥ ardhacandreṇa ciccheda sajyaṃ saviśikhaṃ tadā
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, O great king, cut Gautama's great bow, strung and with arrow fitted, with a crescent-headed shaft.

sanskrit: tasya kruddhaḥ kṛpo rājañ śaktiṃ cikṣepa dāruṇām svarṇadaṇḍām akuṇṭhāgrāṃ karmāraparimārjitām
english: At this Kṛpa, in wrath, O king, hurled a dreadful spear, gold-shafted, sharp of point, polished by the smith.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ ciccheda śikhaṇḍī bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ sāpatan medinīṃ dīptā bhāsayantī mahāprabhā
english: That oncoming spear Śikhaṇḍin cut with many arrows, and it fell blazing to the earth, lighting it up with its great splendor.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya gautamo rathināṃ varaḥ prācchādayac chitair bāṇair mahārāja śikhaṇḍinam
english: Then taking up another bow, the descendant of Gautama, that best of chariot-warriors, covered Śikhaṇḍin with sharp arrows, O great king.

sanskrit: sa chādyamānaḥ samare gautamena yaśasvinā vyaṣīdata rathopasthe śikhaṇḍī rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Overwhelmed in battle by the illustrious descendant of Gautama, Śikhaṇḍin, that best of chariot-warriors, sank down upon the floor of his car.

sanskrit: sīdantaṃ cainam ālokya kṛpaḥ śāradvato yudhi ājaghne bahubhir bāṇair jighāṃsann iva bhārata
english: And seeing him sinking down in the fight, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat smote him with many arrows, as if eager to slay him, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vimukhaṃ taṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā yājñaseniṃ mahāratham pāñcālāḥ somakāś caiva parivavruḥ samantataḥ
english: Seeing that son of Yajñasena, the great chariot-warrior, turned away in the battle, the Pāñcālas and the Somakas surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putrāś ca parivavrur dvijottamam mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ tato yuddham abhūt punaḥ
english: And likewise your sons, with a great army, surrounded that best of the twice-born; and so the battle was joined again.

sanskrit: rathānāṃ ca raṇe rājann anyonyam abhidhāvatām babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo meghānāṃ nadatām iva
english: And of the chariots rushing against one another in the battle, O king, there arose a tumultuous din like that of roaring clouds.

sanskrit: dravatāṃ sādināṃ caiva gajānāṃ ca viśāṃ pate anyonyam abhito rājan krūram āyodhanaṃ babhau
english: Of the rushing horsemen and the elephants too, O lord of peoples, set against one another, O king, the field of battle showed a cruel sight.

sanskrit: pattīnāṃ dravatāṃ caiva padaśabdena medinī akampata mahārāja bhayatrasteva cāṅganā
english: At the tramp of the running foot-soldiers the earth trembled, O great king, like a woman shuddering with fear.

sanskrit: rathā rathān samāsādya pradrutā vegavattaram nyagṛhṇan bahavo rājañ śalabhān vāyasā iva
english: Chariots, falling upon chariots and rushing on with greater speed, seized them in numbers, O king, as crows seize locusts.

sanskrit: tathā gajān prabhinnāṃś ca suprabhinnā mahāgajāḥ tasminn eva pade yattā nigṛhṇanti sma bhārata
english: And likewise the great elephants in full rut, holding their ground in that very spot, seized the rutting elephants, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sādī sādinam āsādya padātī ca padātinam samāsādya raṇe 'nyonyaṃ saṃrabdhā nāticakramuḥ
english: Horseman closing with horseman, and foot-soldier with foot-soldier, joining battle in their fury, did not pass one another by.

sanskrit: dhāvatāṃ dravatāṃ caiva punar āvartatām api babhūva tatra sainyānāṃ śabdaḥ sutumulo niśi
english: Of the running, the fleeing, and those who turned back again, there arose there among the hosts a most tumultuous din in the night.

sanskrit: dīpyamānāḥ pradīpāś ca rathavāraṇavājiṣu adṛśyanta mahārāja maholkā iva khāc cyutāḥ
english: And the blazing lamps upon the chariots, elephants, and horses appeared, O great king, like great meteors fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: sā niśā bharataśreṣṭha pradīpair avabhāsitā divasapratimā rājan babhūva raṇamūrdhani
english: That night, O best of the Bhāratas, lit up by the lamps, became like day, O king, at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: ādityena yathā vyāptaṃ tamo loke praṇaśyati tathā naṣṭaṃ tamo ghoraṃ dīpair dīptair alaṃkṛtam
english: As the darkness pervaded by the sun perishes in the world, so the terrible darkness vanished, adorned by the blazing lamps.

sanskrit: śastrāṇāṃ kavacānāṃ ca maṇīnāṃ ca mahātmanām antardadhuḥ prabhāḥ sarvā dīpais tair avabhāsitāḥ
english: The radiance of the weapons, the armor, and the jewels of those great-souled ones was all swallowed up, outshone by those lamps.

sanskrit: tasmin kolāhale yuddhe vartamāne niśāmukhe avadhīt samare putraṃ pitā bharatasattama
english: In that uproarious battle raging at the onset of night, a father slew his son in the fight, O most excellent of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: putraś ca pitaraṃ mohāt sakhāyaṃ ca sakhā tathā saṃbandhinaṃ ca saṃbandhī svasrīyaṃ cāpi mātulaḥ
english: And a son in his bewilderment slew his father, a friend his friend, a kinsman his kinsman, and an uncle his sister's son.

sanskrit: sve svān pare parāṃś cāpi nijaghnur itaretaram nirmaryādam abhūd yuddhaṃ rātrau ghoraṃ bhayāvaham
english: Friends slew friends and foes slew foes, each striking the other; the battle in the night was without restraint, terrible and fraught with fear.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin sutumule yuddhe vartamāne bhayāvahe dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja droṇam evābhyavartata
english: Saṃjaya said: As that most tumultuous and fearful battle raged on, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, advanced straight against Droṇa.

sanskrit: saṃmṛjāno dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ jyāṃ vikarṣan punaḥ punaḥ abhyavartata droṇasya rathaṃ rukmavibhūṣitam
english: Stroking his excellent bow and drawing its string again and again, he advanced upon Droṇa's chariot, adorned with gold.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tadāyāntaṃ droṇasyāntacikīrṣayā parivavrur mahārāja pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: As Dhṛṣṭadyumna then came on, eager to make an end of Droṇa, the Pāñcālas, together with the Pāṇḍavas, surrounded him, O great king.

sanskrit: tathā parivṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā droṇam ācāryasattamam putrās te sarvato yattā rarakṣur droṇam āhave
english: Seeing Droṇa, that best of preceptors, thus encompassed, your sons, intent on every side, guarded Droṇa in the fray.

sanskrit: balārṇavau tatas tau tu sameyātāṃ niśāmukhe vātoddhūtau kṣubdhasattvau bhairavau sāgarāv iva
english: Then those two oceans of host met at the onset of night, like two dreadful seas lashed by the wind, their creatures churned into turmoil.

sanskrit: tato droṇaṃ mahārāja pāñcālyaḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha hṛdaye tūrṇaṃ siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca
english: Then the prince of the Pāñcālas, O great king, swiftly pierced Droṇa in the heart with five arrows, and uttered a lion's roar.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaḥ pañcaviṃśatyā viddhvā bhārata saṃyuge cicchedānyena bhallena dhanur asya mahāprabham
english: Droṇa, having pierced him with twenty-five shafts in the battle, O Bhārata, cut with another broad-headed arrow his bright-shining bow.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu nirviddho droṇena bharatarṣabha utsasarja dhanus tūrṇaṃ saṃdaśya daśanacchadam
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, sorely pierced by Droṇa, O bull of the Bhāratas, swiftly cast aside that bow, biting his lip.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pratāpavān ādade 'nyad dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ droṇasyāntacikīrṣayā
english: Then, in his wrath, O great king, the mighty Dhṛṣṭadyumna took up another excellent bow, eager to make an end of Droṇa.

sanskrit: vikṛṣya ca dhanuś citram ākarṇāt paravīrahā droṇasyāntakaraṃ ghoraṃ vyasṛjat sāyakaṃ tataḥ
english: And drawing his wondrous bow to his ear, that slayer of hostile heroes then loosed a terrible shaft to make an end of Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa visṛṣṭo balavatā śaro ghoro mahāmṛdhe bhāsayām āsa tat sainyaṃ divākara ivoditaḥ
english: That terrible arrow, loosed by the mighty one in the great battle, lit up that host like the risen sun.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu śaraṃ ghoraṃ devagandharvamānavāḥ svasty astu samare rājan droṇāyety abruvan vacaḥ
english: Seeing that terrible arrow, the gods, Gandharvas, and men spoke these words, O king: "May it be well with Droṇa in the battle."

sanskrit: taṃ tu sāyakam aprāptam ācāryasya rathaṃ prati karṇo dvādaśadhā rājaṃś ciccheda kṛtahastavat
english: But that shaft, before it reached the preceptor's chariot, Karṇa cut into twelve pieces, O king, like one skilled of hand.

sanskrit: sa chinno bahudhā rājan sūtaputreṇa māriṣa nipapāta śaras tūrṇaṃ nikṛttaḥ karṇasāyakaiḥ
english: Cut into many pieces by the charioteer's son, O king, O venerable one, that arrow, severed by Karṇa's shafts, swiftly fell.

sanskrit: chittvā tu samare bāṇaṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ raṇe karṇo vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Having cut that arrow in the battle with his smooth-jointed shafts, Karṇa pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the fight with ten arrows.
